filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.question: In Philippians 1:18, Paul rejoices as long as Christ is proclaimed.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.learningObjective: Observe the cause of Paul's joy.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: By pretext or by truth, Christ proclaimed makes Paul rejoice.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Philippians 1:18: in this I rejoice, he says.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: See the condition of his joy.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:21, tap who Paul's living is.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.learningObjective: Identify the center of Paul's life.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: For him, to live is not a project: it is a person.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the verb; who fills the living comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what dying is for him, not living.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the name after the verb "é".

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.question: According to Philippians 1:21, what does Paul say about living and dying?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: Both halves turn on Christ, not on fear.

feedbackWrong.a: He is sure about both sides of the sentence.
feedbackWrong.b: Dying, for him, is gain, not any kind of failure.
feedbackWrong.d: He does not flee: he judges staying more necessary.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: Compare the two halves of the verse.

options.a: To live is uncertain, and to die is to forget
options.b: To live is to suffer, and to die is to fail
options.c: To live is Christ, and to die is gain
options.d: To live is to flee, and to die is to lose all

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.question: Put Philippians 1:20 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of Paul's hope.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: No shame, Christ exalted, in life or in death.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the hope of not being put to shame.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: The sentence closes with life and death.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:18, what does Paul do when Christ is proclaimed, even by pretext?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.learningObjective: Remember Paul's reaction to the proclamation.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: Christ's proclamation makes Paul rejoice, however it comes.

feedbackWrong.a: He does not fight over the motive: he celebrates the news.
feedbackWrong.b: Tears do not appear: he says he will keep rejoicing.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is his reaction to the gospel announced.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What does Philippians 1:18 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Link Paul's joy to the proclamation of Christ.
filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: Even in prison, he rejoices: the announcement keeps going.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not rage: he says he will keep rejoicing.
feedbackWrong.c: The gospel advances; no end is announced here.

filipenses-sem-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: See his reaction to Christ being announced.

options.a: Joy while Christ is proclaimed
options.b: Anger at those who preach differently
options.c: Sadness at the end of the gospel

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.question: In Philippians 1:23–24, Paul decided to depart because staying in the flesh no longer served the church.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.learningObjective: Understand the dilemma between departing and staying.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: He desires to depart, but judges staying more necessary for them.

feedbackWrong.true: The desire is to depart; his judgment is to stay for their sake.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: Separate his desire from his judgment.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:23, tap the word that shows what Paul feels about departing.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: He feels desire to depart and be with Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the destination of the desire, not the word of feeling.
feedbackWrong.c: That names his tension, not the desire itself.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the verb "sinto" and what comes after.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.question: How does Paul's joy relate to his future in Philippians 1:18–19?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.learningObjective: Relate present joy and future hope.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: Present joy and trust in prayer and the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.a: He trusts prayer and the Spirit, not rivals.
feedbackWrong.b: He already rejoices, in prison, before any release.
feedbackWrong.c: Fear does not rule: there is expectation and hope in him.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: Join today's joy with his hope.

options.a: He leaves the future in his rivals' hands
options.b: He will only rejoice after leaving prison
options.c: He trades joy for fear of judgment
options.d: He rejoices now and trusts the church's prayer

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.question: How do Paul's thoughts connect in Philippians 1:23–24?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: Understand the chain of Paul's dilemma.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: Desire, recognition, and judgment for others: that is the order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the desire he feels.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: The judgment for the church closes the reasoning.

options.a: He desires to depart and be with Christ
options.b: He recognizes that departing would be far better
options.c: He judges staying more necessary for the church

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:24, how does Paul evaluate staying in the flesh for the church's sake?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: The church's good weighs more than his desire.

feedbackWrong.a: Shame is exactly what he hopes not to have.
feedbackWrong.b: He sees fruit and need in staying, not uselessness.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is a judgment about others' good.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What links Philippians 1:23 to 2 Corinthians 5:8?
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Relate Paul's desire in two letters.
filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, to depart is to be present with the Lord.

feedbackWrong.a: There is no fear: there is desire and trust in both.
feedbackWrong.b: The mission continues; the shared point is being with him.

filipenses-cam-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: Compare the destination of departing in both texts.

options.a: Fear of leaving the body
options.b: End of the mission on earth
options.c: Desire to be with the Lord

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.question: Philippians 1:21 shows death without being final loss, because living and dying turn on Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.feedbackCorrect: Christ is the center of both sides: life and death.

feedbackWrong.false: He calls dying gain, not final loss.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-01.hint: See what occupies the center of the sentence.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.question: In Philippians 1:20, tap where Christ will be exalted, according to Paul.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text where Christ is exalted.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.feedbackCorrect: Alive or dead, his body is Christ's stage.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the manner of proclamation, not its place.
feedbackWrong.b: That is his feeling, not where Christ appears.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-02.hint: Look for the place after "engrandecido no".

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.question: What reading do Philippians 1:20–21 support about Paul's life?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.feedbackCorrect: In both outcomes, what matters is Christ exalted.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not measure success by release: Christ is the measure.
feedbackWrong.c: Staying is a judgment of love for the church, not lack of faith.
feedbackWrong.d: He calls dying gain, not failure.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-03.hint: See what is the same in his life and death.

options.a: Christ is the center in life and also in death
options.b: Success is leaving prison at any cost
options.c: Staying alive proves he lacked faith to depart
options.d: Dying would be the total failure of the gospel

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 1:18–23?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.learningObjective: See Christ as the thread of the whole passage.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.feedbackCorrect: From proclamation to being with Christ: the thread is the same name.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with joy at the proclamation in prison.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-04.hint: Being with Christ is the arrival point.

options.a: Christ proclaimed makes imprisoned Paul rejoice
options.b: Christ exalted in him, alive or dead
options.c: Being with Christ is the best destination

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.question: In Philippians 1:21, what does Paul say dying is for him?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries Paul's hope.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.feedbackCorrect: Being with Christ makes death gain, not loss.

feedbackWrong.b: Loss is the opposite of what he declares here.
feedbackWrong.c: Punishment does not appear: he speaks of being with Christ.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-05.hint: It is a word from the world of gains.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.question: What links Philippians 1:20 to Galatians 2:20?
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.learningObjective: Link "to live is Christ" to the faith of Galatians.
filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.feedbackCorrect: In Galatians, Paul says the same: I no longer live; Christ lives.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts put Christ right at the center of life.
feedbackWrong.c: The law is not the declared center in these verses.

filipenses-pro-fp-01-alegria-06.hint: See who lives, according to both texts.

options.a: Life without Christ at the center
options.b: Christ lives in me
options.c: Law as the center of life

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.question: In Philippians 2:3, Paul told each one to consider himself superior to all others.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the opposite: consider others superior to yourself.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Philippians 2:3: humility looks toward the other.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See the direction of considering in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:8, tap how far Christ's obedience went.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.learningObjective: Identify the limit of Christ's obedience.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: His obedience did not stop short of the hardest end.

feedbackWrong.a: Man is the form he took, not the limit of obedience.
feedbackWrong.c: That specifies the kind of death, after the limit named.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the word right after "até à".

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.question: According to Philippians 2:8, how did Christ humble himself?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: His descent goes as far as obedience on the cross.

feedbackWrong.a: He took on suffering; he did not refuse it.
feedbackWrong.b: He did not flee: he gave himself in obedience.
feedbackWrong.c: The cross exposed, not hid, his mission.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: See the end of the downward path.

options.a: Refusing any kind of suffering
options.b: Fleeing from people who rejected him
options.c: Hiding who he was until old age
options.d: Becoming obedient unto death on a cross

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.question: Put Philippians 2:7 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of Christ's descent.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: He empties himself, becomes a servant, and is made like men.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with his emptying of himself.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The order begins with him emptying himself.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:7, what form did Christ take when he emptied himself?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: The one who was God takes the place of one who serves.

feedbackWrong.a: Judgment is not the form he takes when he descends.
feedbackWrong.b: He will be recognized as King, but here he takes another place.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is the place of one who serves others.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What does Philippians 2:5 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Link the church's life to the mind of Christ.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: The remedy for rivalry is to have the mind of Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: Christ drew near and served; he did not keep distance.
feedbackWrong.c: Rivalry and vanity are the problem, not the remedy.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See whose mind is asked for.

options.a: Safe distance from others
options.b: The same mind of Christ
options.c: Pride that wins debates

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.question: In Philippians 2:9, God exalted Christ because he humbled himself unto death on a cross.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.learningObjective: Understand the link between humiliation and exaltation.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: "Por isso" links the exaltation to his obedient humiliation.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse begins by linking exaltation to his descent.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See the first two words of the verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:3, tap the little word that turns rivalry's order into humility.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: Nothing from rivalry; with humility, says the turn.

feedbackWrong.b: That opens the prohibition; it does not make the turn.
feedbackWrong.c: That is one of the evils forbidden, not the turn.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the short conjunction before "humildade".

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.question: How does Christ's path in Philippians 2:6–8 answer the rivalry of 2:3?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.learningObjective: Relate Christ's example to the church's life.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: The opposite of rivalry: letting go and serving unto the cross.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not fight for superiority: he descends to servant.
feedbackWrong.c: The one who serves here is he, not those around him.
feedbackWrong.d: He was made like men; he did not withdraw from them.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: Compare clinging to rights with emptying oneself.

options.a: Instead of clinging to his right, he made himself a servant
options.b: He defeated rivals by showing he was superior to all
options.c: He demanded that everyone serve him first on earth
options.d: He left people behind to live alone in heaven

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.question: How does Christ's descent chain together in Philippians 2:6–8?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: Understand the stages of Christ's descent.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: Not clinging, emptying himself, and obeying unto the cross.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what he did not insist on holding.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The cross is the lowest point of the descent.

options.a: He does not cling to being equal with God
options.b: He empties himself and takes the form of a servant
options.c: He obeys unto death on a cross

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:5, what must the church have in itself, as was in Christ?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.learningObjective: Understand what the church must imitate in Christ.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: It is not only to admire: it is to have the same way of feeling.

feedbackWrong.a: Debating from rivalry is precisely the problem.
feedbackWrong.b: Fear is not what Paul tells them to copy from Christ.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is Christ's inward way toward others.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What links Philippians 2:7 to Mark 10:45?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Relate the form of a servant to Jesus' words.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus himself said: he came not to be served, but to serve.

feedbackWrong.a: He serves even to giving his life; he flees from nothing.
feedbackWrong.b: Both texts invert greatness by domination.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came for.

options.a: A servant who flees from suffering
options.b: Greatness by dominating others
options.c: The Son of Man came to serve

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.question: Philippians 2:6–7 teaches that Jesus stopped being God when he took the form of a servant.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.learningObjective: Interpret the descent without erasing who Christ is.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: He existed in the form of God and takes that of a servant: addition, not swap.

feedbackWrong.true: The hymn keeps both forms over the same Christ.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See what he already was before descending.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:6, tap what Christ already existed as, before emptying himself.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text who Christ was before the descent.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: The descent starts from above: he already existed as God.

feedbackWrong.b: That speaks of the equality he did not use for himself.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what he did not consider doing, not what he was.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the first description of him in the verse.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.question: What reading do Philippians 2:6–9 support about humility and exaltation?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the hymn supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: The descent to servant ends in exaltation given by the Father.

feedbackWrong.b: The hymn begins by affirming that he existed as God.
feedbackWrong.c: Exaltation answers obedience, not luck.
feedbackWrong.d: Humility here is serving the other, not hating yourself.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: Link "por isso" to the prior descent.

options.a: Whoever humbles himself as a servant is exalted by God
options.b: Christ is only a moral example, without being God
options.c: Exaltation is a prize of luck for a few
options.d: Humility is thinking that you are worth nothing

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 2:6–11?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: See the full arc of the hymn of Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: From God to servant, from servant to Lord confessed by all.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who he was before descending.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The universal confession closes the hymn.

options.a: The Son exists in the form of God
options.b: He descends to an obedient servant unto the cross
options.c: Every tongue confesses him as Lord

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:9, what did God grant Christ above all others?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.learningObjective: Remember the center of Christ's exaltation.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: At his name every knee will bow, says the hymn.

feedbackWrong.a: Throne is not the hymn's word in this sentence.
feedbackWrong.b: No temple is granted in this exaltation.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is before him that every knee bows.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What links Philippians 2:7 to John 1:14?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Link Christ's descent to the incarnation in John.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: John says the same mystery: the divine Word became flesh.

feedbackWrong.a: Flesh is taken on in love, not as a prison.
feedbackWrong.b: He remains God when he becomes flesh, in both texts.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See what the Word became in John.

options.a: Flesh as a prison of the spirit
options.b: God gives up being God
options.c: The Word became flesh

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: In Philippians 4:11, Paul says he learned to live content in every situation.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: Learned, not automatic: content in every situation.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Philippians 4:11: that is exactly what he declares.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: See the verb "aprendi" in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:12, tap how Paul knows how to be when he goes through being brought low.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: He knows both extremes: brought low and honored.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the opposite extreme from what the question asks.
feedbackWrong.b: That is abundance of food, not being brought low.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for the first extreme named in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: According to Philippians 4:12, what has Paul already experienced in life?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: Both sides of life entered his experience.

feedbackWrong.a: Inheritance is not cited: he speaks of experience.
feedbackWrong.b: He also cites being honored and abundance.
feedbackWrong.d: He also cites hunger and scarcity, not only plenty.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Pay attention to the pairs of opposites.

options.a: Wealth inherited from his birth
options.b: Only scarcity, never being honored
options.c: Plenty and hunger, abundance and scarcity
options.d: Only plenty, never going through need

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: Put Philippians 4:12 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: Recognize the order of the extremes named.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Brought low, honored, and the extremes of plenty and hunger.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the first "sei o que é" of the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The list begins with being brought low.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:11, how did Paul learn to live in any situation?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.learningObjective: Remember the central word of contentment.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: Neither plenty nor lack takes that state from him.

feedbackWrong.a: He speaks and writes about this; he did not stay silent.
feedbackWrong.c: Anxiety is the opposite of what he learned.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the name of this whole scene.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What does Philippians 4:11 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: Help gladdens him, but his contentment does not depend on it.

feedbackWrong.a: He thanks openly, with no shame at receiving.
feedbackWrong.b: He rejoices at the help, with no despair at all.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See what he says he learned.

options.a: Shame at needing others
options.b: Despair because of the help
options.c: Contentment in every situation

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: In Philippians 4:13–14, Paul thanks the church for sharing in his trouble, even while saying he can do all things in Christ.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.learningObjective: Understand strength in Christ together with receiving help.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: Strength in Christ and gratitude for help go together in him.

feedbackWrong.false: He affirms both things, one in each verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: Read the two verses as one speech.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:12, tap the little word that links plenty and hunger in the same experience.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.learningObjective: Recognize the link between the extremes lived.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: The same life held both extremes named.

feedbackWrong.b: That summarizes circumstances, without linking the extremes.
feedbackWrong.c: That is one of the extremes, not the word that links them.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for the word that pairs with "quanto".

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: How does Philippians 4:11 help us understand "I can do all things" in 4:13?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.learningObjective: Relate Philippians 4:13 to its immediate context.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: The context rules: all things are plenty and scarcity.

feedbackWrong.a: He just cited hunger and scarcity he lived.
feedbackWrong.b: Consumer desires do not appear in the passage.
feedbackWrong.d: He receives help with gratitude, not pride.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Look at the verses around the famous line.

options.a: A promise never to face need again
options.b: Power to get any object desired
options.c: Strength to live content in plenty and in lack
options.d: Ability to live without anyone's help

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: How does Paul's reasoning chain in Philippians 4:11–13?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: Understand the chain up to Philippians 4:13.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Learning, extremes lived, and the source of strength.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The source of strength closes the reasoning.

options.a: He learns contentment in any situation
options.b: He goes through plenty, hunger, and scarcity
options.c: He can do all things in the one who strengthens him

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:10, what did the Philippians finally do for Paul, according to him?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.learningObjective: Understand the renewed help from the Philippians.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: Help returned because they remembered him again.

feedbackWrong.a: They already remembered before; opportunity was missing.
feedbackWrong.c: No judgment appears in this letter of gratitude.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the reason for his joy in the verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What links Philippians 4:11 to 1 Timothy 6:8?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.learningObjective: Relate contentment in two of Paul's letters.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: Food and clothing suffice: contentment with enough.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts teach braking the chase for more.
feedbackWrong.b: Having little is no shame in either text.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See what is enough in both texts.

options.a: Endless chase for more goods
options.b: Shame at having little in life
options.c: Contentment with enough

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: Philippians 4:13 promises that the believer can achieve any desire he has, without limits.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: In context, all things is living in plenty and in lack.

feedbackWrong.true: Read 4:11–12 first: the strength is for contentment, not desires.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: Check the immediate context of the line.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:13, tap the phrase that shows Paul's strength does not come from himself.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text the source of Paul's strength.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: Strength is received from another: from the one who strengthens him.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the capacity, not its source.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the reach, not where the strength comes from.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for who gives, at the end of the verse.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: What reading do Philippians 4:11–12 support about contentment?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the passage supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: Learned in Christ, he goes through both extremes.

feedbackWrong.a: He receives help gratefully: the things coexist.
feedbackWrong.b: He cites hunger and scarcity as real experience of his.
feedbackWrong.d: He feels and learns; it is not absence of feeling.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Join learning, extremes, and the source of strength.

options.a: Contentment makes any help unnecessary
options.b: Whoever has faith never faces real scarcity
options.c: It is possible to be whole in plenty and in lack, in him
options.d: Contentment is feeling nothing in the face of loss

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 4:10–13?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: See help, contentment, and Christ in the right order.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Help received, independent contentment, and strength in him.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the help that began arriving again.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The source of strength is the close of the passage.

options.a: The church remembers him and helps again
options.b: He declares contentment that does not depend on that
options.c: He points to Christ as the source of strength

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:12, which extreme of lack does Paul say he already knows by experience?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: His contentment was tested precisely in lack.

feedbackWrong.b: That is recognition, not material lack.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the extreme of surplus, not of lack.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the opposite of abundance at the end of the list.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What links Philippians 4:13 to 2 Corinthians 12:9?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.learningObjective: Link the strength of Philippians to Paul's thorn.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: In both, God's power shows itself precisely in weakness.

feedbackWrong.b: The strength is his in us, not self-sufficiency.
feedbackWrong.c: Weakness becomes a place of grace, not of punishment.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See where God's power is made perfect.

options.a: God's strength in weakness
options.b: One's own strength without depending
options.c: Weakness as final punishment

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-01.question: In this challenge, Paul asks in Philippians 2:3 that each person consider himself superior to others.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The order is the reverse: consider others superior to yourself.

feedbackWrong.true: The text tells you to see the other as superior, in humility.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-01.hint: Remember the direction of humility in the letter.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-02.question: In Philippians 1:21, tap who Paul's living is.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review the center of Paul's life.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: The letter's summary begins with that name at the center.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the other side of the sentence, not the living.
feedbackWrong.c: That defines his dying, not his living.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-02.hint: Look for the name in the middle of the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-03.question: In Paul's summary in Philippians 1:21, living and dying are defined as what?
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Review the central declaration of Philippians 1.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: It is the line that sums up his joy in prison.

feedbackWrong.a: Whether staying or departing, his center is not the prison.
feedbackWrong.b: He has declared certainty about both sides.
feedbackWrong.d: He calls dying gain, not defeat.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-03.hint: Recover the letter's most famous line.

options.a: To live is prison, and to die is escape
options.b: To live is doubt, and to die is nothing
options.c: To live is Christ, and to die is gain
options.d: To live is fear, and to die is defeat

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-04.question: Put Philippians 2:7 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the sequence of Christ's descent.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Emptying himself, form of a servant, and human likeness.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with his emptying of himself.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-04.hint: Follow the descent step by step.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-05.question: In Philippians 2:7, Christ emptied himself taking the form of one who serves, called what?
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: It is the form that sums up the mind of Christ in the letter.

feedbackWrong.b: Judgment is not the form he takes here.
feedbackWrong.c: Lord is what he will be confessed as later, in exaltation.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-05.hint: It is the position of one who serves others.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-06.question: What does Philippians 4:13 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Review the source of Paul's strength.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: The strength is not his: it comes from the one who strengthens him.

feedbackWrong.b: He receives strength and help; he is not self-sufficient.
feedbackWrong.c: No luck: there is a personal source declared.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-06.hint: See from whom comes what he can do.

options.a: Christ's strength in every situation
options.b: One's own strength with no one else
options.c: Luck that changes with time

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-07.question: In Philippians 2:9, tap what God granted Christ above all.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-07.learningObjective: Review the center of Christ's exaltation.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: Before that name, every knee will bow.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the one who grants, not what is granted.
feedbackWrong.b: That says how much he was exalted, not what he received.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-07.hint: Look for the gift given in the exaltation.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-08.question: Put Philippians 1:20 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: No shame, Christ exalted, alive or dead.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the hope of having no shame.

filipenses-sem-fp-04-desafio-08.hint: The sentence closes with his two destinies.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-01.question: In Philippians 4:13, Paul guarantees he will achieve any personal desire he has.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: In context, it is strength for contentment, not for desires.

feedbackWrong.true: Read 4:11–12: plenty and scarcity define the all things.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-01.hint: Go back two verses before the line.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-02.question: In Philippians 2:3, tap the conjunction that turns rivalry into humility.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: The turn of the sentence is the turn of life in community.

feedbackWrong.a: That opens the prohibition, without making the turn.
feedbackWrong.c: That is one of the evils to leave behind.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-02.hint: Look for the little word before "humildade".

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-03.question: How does Christ's example in Philippians 2:5–8 attack the church's rivalry?
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Review the hymn's application to the community.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Against fighting for the top, Christ descends to servant.

feedbackWrong.a: The one who serves is the greatest of all, Christ himself.
feedbackWrong.b: The text tells each one to care also for what is others'.
feedbackWrong.d: He does not defeat rivalry by rivaling better.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-03.hint: Compare fighting for the top with descending to servant.

options.a: Proving that serving is for the weakest
options.b: Telling each one to care only for his own life
options.c: Showing that greatness is descending to serve
options.d: Teaching to win debates with more force

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-04.question: How does Christ's descent chain together in this challenge?
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: Review the stages of the mind of Christ.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Letting go, serving, and obeying unto the cross.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what he did not hold onto for himself.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-04.hint: The cross remains the final point.

options.a: He lets go of clinging to what is his
options.b: He takes the place of one who serves all
options.c: He obeys unto the most humiliating death

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-05.question: In Philippians 4:11, Paul learned to live in what way in any situation?
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: It is the learning that sustains the end of the letter.

feedbackWrong.a: He draws near to the church with gratitude, not distance.
feedbackWrong.c: Haste is not cited in this learning of his.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-05.hint: It is the title of what he learned.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-06.question: What links Philippians 2:7 to John 1:14?
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Review the link between the hymn and the incarnation.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: The same mystery: the divine becomes real human flesh.

feedbackWrong.a: The direction is reverse: God descends; men do not ascend.
feedbackWrong.b: He does not abandon who he is when he becomes flesh.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-06.hint: See what the Word became in John.

options.a: Men become gods by effort
options.b: God abandons an empty heaven
options.c: The Word became flesh

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-07.question: In Philippians 1:23, tap the word that names what Paul feels about departing.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-07.learningObjective: Review the dilemma of departing and staying.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: His desire points toward being with Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: That names the tension, not the desire felt.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the desired action, not the feeling named.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-07.hint: Look for what he feels, declared in the verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-08.question: How does Paul's contentment advance in Philippians 4:11–13?
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Review the path up to Philippians 4:13.
filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Learn, go through extremes, and depend on him.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the learning he declares.

filipenses-cam-fp-04-desafio-08.hint: The strength received closes the advance.

options.a: Contentment learned in any scenario
options.b: Extremes of plenty and lack gone through
options.c: Strength received from the one who strengthens him

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-01.question: In Philippians, joy, humility, and contentment have the same center, which is Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-01.learningObjective: Interpret the thematic unity of the letter.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: Imprisoned, as servant, or in lack, the center does not change: Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: The letter's three themes meet in that name.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-01.hint: Look for the name common to the three themes.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-02.question: In Philippians 1:20, tap where Christ will be exalted in Paul's life.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-02.learningObjective: Review where Christ appears in Paul's life.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Alive or dead, his body shows Christ as great.

feedbackWrong.b: That is his feeling, not the place.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the manner, not the place of exalting.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-02.hint: Look for the place after "engrandecido no".

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-03.question: What reading best summarizes the letter to the Philippians in this challenge?
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-03.learningObjective: Choose the synthesis the letter supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: One center alone sustains the letter's three themes.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul lives all of this precisely imprisoned and in lack.
feedbackWrong.c: His joy is born from the Christ who humbled himself.
feedbackWrong.d: He reads prison as Christ's stage, not abandonment.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-03.hint: Join the three themes in one common center.

options.a: Without good circumstances, no one can live the faith
options.b: With Christ at the center, there is joy, service, and contentment
options.c: Humility and joy are themes that contradict each other
options.d: Paul's prison proves that God abandoned him

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-04.question: What sequence reveals the whole arc of Philippians?
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-04.learningObjective: See the letter's arc from the start to the hymn.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Proclamation, descent, and universal confession of the Lord.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the proclamation that makes Paul rejoice.

options.a: Christ proclaimed makes even a prisoner rejoice
options.b: The mind of Christ descends to the place of a servant
options.c: The Father exalts and every tongue confesses

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-05.question: In Philippians 4:13, what does Paul receive from the one who sustains him in everything?
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-05.learningObjective: Review Paul's resource in every situation.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: It is his resource in plenty and also in scarcity.

feedbackWrong.a: Fame is not what he seeks or receives here.
feedbackWrong.c: He keeps working; he does not receive time off.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-05.hint: It is what the other gives him, at the end of the line.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-06.question: What links Philippians 1:21 to Romans 14:8?
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-06.learningObjective: Link the summary of Philippians to that of Romans.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: In Romans, Paul sums up the same: we are his, alive or dead.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts hand life and death over to the Lord.
feedbackWrong.c: Dying is gain and being with him, not an empty end.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-06.hint: See to whom life and death belong in Romans.

options.a: We live and die for the Lord
options.b: Life and death with no lord at all
options.c: Death as an absolute final point

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-07.question: In Philippians 2:5, tap what must exist in the church as it existed in Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-07.learningObjective: Review what the church copies from Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: It is not imitating loose gestures: it is the same way of feeling.

feedbackWrong.b: He is the model; what is copied comes before.
feedbackWrong.c: That is whom Paul addresses, not what to copy.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-08.question: What sequence reveals the logic of joy that remains?
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-08.learningObjective: Understand the logic of Paul's joy.
filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Center in life, gain in death, and service to others.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the definition of living for Paul.

filipenses-pro-fp-04-desafio-08.hint: Serving the church is his practical conclusion.

options.a: To live is Christ, even inside prison
options.b: To die is gain, without fear of the outcome
options.c: To stay is to serve the church with a whole heart
